newsitem.title: UK: J. Sainsbury to offer insurance products.
newsitem.headline: J. Sainsbury to offer insurance products.

text.p: British supermarket retailer J. Sainsbury Plc said on Friday that its Homebase do-it-yourself unit would offer insurance products to customers as it teamed up with broker Willis Corroon.

Sainsbury said Homebase's customers would be offered home and contents insurance, garden insurance and personal accident insurance with details to be released at the launch to the public in early February.

The service will be available to all Homebase customers with a launch to its two million loyalty card holders and will be provided by a panel made up of Royal & Sun Alliance, Guardian Royal Exchange, Norwich Union, Eagle Star and Lloyds of London.
"We believe that the Homebase brand values can make a real difference in the home insurance market," said Mike Samuel, Homebase head of marketing.
Sainsbury said major features of the products would be 250 pounds emergency cover, cover for home removal, Christmas, birthdays and accidental damage to televisions and satellites.
Sainsbury became the first supermarket to announce plans to launch banking services in October 1996 when it teamed up with Bank of Scotland to form Sainsbury's Bank.
